The Spanish and Cuban types have six courses of doubled strings in unison, the Philippine type fourteen strings, some single or in threes. Beginners can start by tuning in fourths; the Spanish type sounds an octave lower than the bandurria, while the Cuban type is shorter and higher. Practise by sounding each course of doubled strings in turn, then join a Spanish or Philippine rondalla alongside the guitar and bandurria.

西班牙琉特琴主要出現在西班牙、古巴與菲律賓的民間弦樂合奏中，常與吉他、班杜里亞琴: The Spanish lute appears mainly in the folk string ensembles of Spain, Cuba and the Philippines, often grouped with the guitar and bandurria, and also in the rondalla string ensemble. The Cuban version can be heard in the playing of Barbarito Torres, a member of the Buena Vista Social Club, which shows its use in plucked ensembles and folk music settings.
西班牙琉特琴是撥片撥弦的弦鳴樂器，屬西特恩琴族。西班牙與古巴版本有六組同度雙弦，: The Spanish lute is a plucked chordophone of the cittern family. The Spanish and Cuban versions have six courses of doubled strings in unison; the Philippine version has fourteen strings, in single, double and triple courses. Its tuning is mostly in fourths, and it sounds an octave lower than the bandurria; the bandurria has a smaller body and a shorter neck. The Cuban version has a shorter sounding length and is tuned higher; the Philippine version is a note lower than the Spanish. The source does not record how volume is controlled.
西班牙琉特琴為撥弦弦鳴樂器，名稱源自阿拉伯語「烏德」，字面意為「木材」，但歸於西: The Spanish lute is a plucked chordophone whose name comes from the Arabic 'ud, literally wood, but it belongs to the cittern family. It spread from Spain and is also found in Cuban, Philippine and other overseas communities. It is traditionally used in folk string ensembles such as the rondalla, alongside the guitar and bandurria, tuned in fourths and sounding an octave below the bandurria. There are regional variants: Spanish and Cuban instruments mostly have six courses of doubled strings in unison, the Philippine instrument fourteen strings, some single or in threes; the Cuban instrument has a shorter sounding length, is tuned higher, and its body sometimes differs.
西班牙琉特琴琴身採用共鳴腔設計，面板多用雲杉或松木製作，背板與側板則採用玫瑰木、: The body uses a resonating cavity: the soundboard is mostly spruce or pine, the back and sides a hardwood such as rosewood, walnut or maple, to strengthen the resonance and warm the timbre. The neck is mahogany or maple and the fingerboard ebony, for durability and projection. The tuning pegs are usually wood or bone, and the strings nylon or metal-wound. The joints use traditional mortise-and-tenon work, and inside there are soundbars and braces to optimise the acoustics.
西班牙琉特琴（Laúd）是源自西班牙的撥片彈撥弦鳴樂器，H-S編號321.322: The Spanish lute (Laúd) is a plucked chordophone from Spain, H-S 321.322, in the cittern family. The Spanish and Cuban versions have six courses of double strings in unison, twelve strings in all; the Philippine version has fourteen, some single or in threes. It is traditionally used in folk string ensembles such as the Spanish or Philippine rondalla, usually together with the guitar and bandurria.
